body: Thanks for letting us know about this. @martijnvg do you happen to remember offhand why we don't currently support data streams for the enrich policy indices?

An enrich policy should just be able to work with a data stream, just like when when an index expression or alias is provided.
I think it just needs to be enabled, but I don't see a technical reason this can't work.

However I do think there is a general concern with using a data stream (just defining an index expression/alias that matches with many indices) that the enrich index will contain a lot of data. The idea is that a relative small data set is used as reference data that can be used to enrich documents at ingest time. The enrich policy periodically moves the reference data to an one shard enrich index. All the data of a data stream could simply not fit in it? Even if it does that execution of the enrich policy could take a long time. But this is already a concern when an index expression is used that matches with many indices. Just something to think about.

Curious on the status of this. I would like to see data streams as an option for Enrich policies. To me there is no difference between a wildcard set of indices via an index pattern vs a data steams.

https://github.com/elastic/kibana/issues/178829

We discussed this today and decided that we should support data streams. I think this can be treated as a bug (either the message is bad, or we should support data streams; we're going with the later).

issue.body:
Previously when someone tried to use a data stream in the `indices` keyword for an enrich policy, an exception would be thrown. This commit changes the resolution so that data streams can be used.

Resolves #98836

issue.body:
**Describe the feature:**
I would like to use a data stream as source for enrichment. Today the indices or the data stream cannot be populated in the UI in Kibana to create the policy. However, using the API we can create an Enrich policy that uses a wildcard. We can even see past enrich policies in the Kibana UI that show that this is possible via the API but not the UI:

![image](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/assets/5582679/245c0933-b8af-4dde-b3e3-d4aab6565fd0)

**Describe a specific use case for the feature:**
The use case is to easily use multiple indices for an enrich policy or if it is part of a data stream - This will always make sure you can hit the index even if the name is not static.
